title: Growth and rates

blocks.heading: Growth and rates
blocks.text: Population changes through births, deaths and net migration; comparable rates allow populations of different sizes to be assessed. Natural increase excludes migration. Higher population level differs from faster increase: compare differences or rates over equal intervals, not the largest final value alone.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Growth rate
blocks.text: Population growth rate measures change in population over a period relative to its starting population, expressed as a percentage for that period. Use total change including migration where appropriate. A growth rate can fall while population still rises if the rate remains positive.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Crude birth rate
blocks.text: Crude birth rate is live births during a year per thousand people in the population. Use births divided by the relevant population, multiplied by 1,000. It differs from births per woman and from a total number of births.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Death rate
blocks.text: The crude death rate measures deaths during a year per thousand people in the population. A crude rate is influenced by age structure as well as health conditions, so a higher rate does not by itself prove worse services.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Infant mortality
blocks.text: Infant mortality rate is deaths before the first birthday per thousand live births, for a stated period. Its denominator is live births, not total population; compare definitions and periods before interpreting a difference.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Demographic transition model
blocks.text: The demographic transition model simplifies changes in birth and death rates and consequent natural population growth during development. The broad four-stage account moves from high birth/death rates, through falling deaths then falling births, towards low rates. It is a model, not an identical timetable for every country; migration is not its central mechanism.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Apply the measure
blocks.text: Describe this fictional series over equal intervals: A grows from 100 to 120 thousand; B from 300 to 310 thousand. B remains larger, but A increases by 20 thousand versus B’s 10 thousand. Level and absolute increase therefore give different comparisons.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
blocks.text: Connect population evidence to Health (7.2), Education (7.3) and Urbanisation (4.2). Check dates, boundaries, denominators and units before explaining what a pattern supports.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
